Subsection.Text: Where the chief depreciable properties of a taxpayer are included in Class 2, 4 or 17 in Schedule II, the taxpayer may elect to include in Class 2, 4 or 17 in Schedule II, as the case may be, a property that would otherwise be included in another class in Schedule II and that was acquired by him before May 26, 1976 for the purpose of gaining or producing income from the same business as that for which those properties otherwise included in the said Class 2, 4 or 17 were acquired.

Heading.TitleText: Elections to Include Properties in Class 8

Subsection.Label: (2a)
Subsection.Text: In respect of properties otherwise included in Class 19 or 21 in Schedule II, a taxpayer may, by letter attached to the return of his income for a taxation year filed with the Minister in accordance with section 150 of the Act, elect to include in Class 8 in Schedule II all properties of the said Class 19 or all properties of the said Class 21, as the case may be, owned by him at the commencement of the year.

Heading.TitleText: Elections to Include Properties in Class 37

Subsection.Label: (2b)
Subsection.Text: In respect of properties that would have been included in Class 37 in Schedule II had they been acquired after the date on which Class 37 became effective, a taxpayer may, by letter attached to the return of his income for a taxation year filed with the Minister in accordance with section 150 of the Act, elect to include in Class 37 all such properties acquired by the taxpayer before that date.

Subsection.Label: (2c)
Subsection.Text: Where a taxpayer has acquired, after May 25, 1976, all or any part of a property of a class in Schedule II (in this subsection referred to as “present class”) and the property or part thereof, if it had been acquired before May 26, 1976, would have been property of a different class in Schedule II (in this subsection referred to as the “former class”) and

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: he was obligated to acquire the property under the terms of an agreement in writing entered into before May 26, 1976,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: he commenced the construction, manufacture or production of the property before May 26, 1976 or the construction, manufacture or production of the property was commenced under an agreement in writing entered into by him before May 26, 1976, or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: he acquired the property on or before December 31, 1976 or he was obligated to acquire the property under the terms of an agreement in writing entered into on or before December 31, 1976, if

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: arrangements, evidenced by writing, respecting the acquisition, construction, manufacture or production of the property had been substantially advanced before May 26, 1976, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: he had, before May 26, 1976, demonstrated a bona fide intention to acquire the property,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: the taxpayer may, by letter attached to the return of his income filed with the Minister in accordance with section 150 of the Act, for the taxation year in which the property was acquired or for the immediately following taxation year, elect to transfer in the year of acquisition

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the property or the part thereof, acquired after May 25, 1976, from the present class to the former class; or

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: the part of the property acquired before May 26, 1976, from the former class to the present class.

Subsection.Label: (2d)
Subsection.Text: Where a taxpayer has

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: disposed of a property (in this subsection referred to as the “former property”) of a class in Schedule II (in this subsection referred to as the “former class”), and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: before the end of the taxation year in which the former property was disposed of, acquired property (in this subsection referred to as the “new property”) of a class in Schedule II (in this subsection referred to as the “present class”) and the present class is neither

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the former class, nor

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a separate class described in section 1101, other than subsection 1101(5d),

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: such that

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if the former property had been acquired at the time that the new property was acquired and from the person from whom the new property was acquired, the former property would have been included in the present class, and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: if the new property had been acquired at the time that the former property was acquired and from the person from whom the former property was acquired, the new property would have been included in the former class,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: the taxpayer may, by letter attached to the return of income of the taxpayer filed with the Minister in accordance with section 150 of the Act in respect of the taxation year in which the former property was disposed of, elect to transfer the former property from the former class to the present class in the year of its disposition and, for greater certainty, the transfer shall be considered to have been made before the disposition of the property.

Subsection.Label: (2e)
Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this Part and Schedule II, where property of a taxpayer would otherwise be included in Class 40 in Schedule II, all such properties owned by the taxpayer shall be transferred from Class 40 to Class 10 immediately after the commencement of the first taxation year of the taxpayer commencing after 1989.

Heading.TitleText: Elections to Include Properties in Class 1, 3 or 6

Subsection.Label: (2f)
Subsection.Text: In respect of properties otherwise included in Class 20 in Schedule II, a taxpayer may, by letter attached to the return of income of the taxpayer for a taxation year filed with the Minister in accordance with section 150 of the Act, elect to include in Class 1, 3 or 6 in Schedule II, as specified in the letter, all properties of Class 20 in Schedule II owned by the taxpayer at the commencement of the year.

Heading.TitleText: Transfers to Class 8, Class 10 or Class 43

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Subsection.Label: (2g)
Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this Part and Schedule II, where one or more properties of a taxpayer are included in a separate class pursuant to an election filed by the taxpayer in accordance with subsection 1101(5q), all the properties in that class immediately after the beginning of the taxpayer’s fifth taxation year beginning after the end of the first taxation year in which a property of the class became available for use by the taxpayer for the purposes of subsection 13(26) of the Act shall be transferred immediately after the beginning of that fifth taxation year from the separate class to the class in which the property would, but for the election, have been included.

Heading.TitleText: Elections Not to Include Properties in Class 44

Subsection.Label: (2h)
Subsection.Text: A taxpayer may, by letter attached to the taxpayer’s return of income filed with the Minister in accordance with section 150 of the Act for the taxation year in which a property was acquired, elect not to include the property in Class 44 in Schedule II.

Heading.TitleText: Election to Include Properties in Class 35

Subsection.Label: (2i)
Subsection.Text: In respect of any property otherwise included in Class 7 in Schedule II because of paragraph (h) of that Class and to which paragraph 1100(1)(z.1a) and subsection 1101(5d), or paragraph 1100(1)(z.1c) and subsection 1101(5d.2), would apply if Class 35 of that Schedule applied to the property, the taxpayer may (by letter attached to the taxpayer’s return of income filed with the Minister in accordance with section 150 of the Act for the taxation year in which the property was acquired) elect to include the property in Class 35 rather than in Class 7.

Subsection.Label: (2j)
Subsection.Text: A taxpayer may, in its return of income filed with the Minister on or before its filing-due date for the taxation year in which a property is acquired, elect not to include the property in any of Classes 54 to 56 in Schedule II, as the case may be.

To be effective in respect of a taxation year, an election under this section must be made not later than the last day on which the taxpayer may file a return of his income for the taxation year in accordance with section 150 of the Act.

An election under paragraph 1102(8)(d) or (9)(d) or this section shall be effective from the first day of the taxation year in respect of which the election is made and shall continue to be effective for all subsequent taxation years.

An election under subsection (1) or (2) shall be made by sending a letter to that effect by registered mail to the Tax Centre at which the taxpayer customarily files the returns required by section 150 of the Act.

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Subsection.Text: Where the taxpayer is an individual and his income for the taxation year includes income from a business the fiscal period of which does not coincide with the calendar year, in respect of the depreciable properties acquired for the purpose of gaining or producing income from the business, a reference in this Part to

Definition.Text: end of the taxation year shall be deemed to be a reference to the end of the fiscal period of the business; (la fin de l’année d’imposition)
taxation year shall be deemed to be a reference to the fiscal period of the business. (l’année d’imposition)

Subsection.Text: In this Part and in Schedule II,

Definition.Text: bitumen development phase of a taxpayer’s oil sands project means a development phase that expands the oil sands project’s capacity to extract and initially process tar sands to produce bitumen or a similar product; (phase de mise en valeur du bitume)

certified feature film means a motion picture film certified by the Minister of Communications to be a film of not less than 75 minutes running time in respect of which all photography or art work specifically required for the production thereof and all film editing therefor were commenced after November 18, 1974, and either the film was completed before May 26, 1976, or the photography or art work was commenced before May 26, 1976, and certified by him to be

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a film the production of which is contemplated in a coproduction agreement entered into between Canada and another country, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a film in respect of which

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the person who performed the duties of producer was a Canadian,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: no fewer than 2/3 in number of all the persons each of whom

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: was a person who performed the duties of director, screenwriter, music composer, art director, picture editor or director of photography, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: was the individual in respect of whose services as an actor or actress in respect of the film the highest remuneration or the second highest remuneration was paid or payable,

ContinuedSubparagraph.Text: were Canadians,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: not less than 75 per cent of the aggregate of the remuneration paid or payable to persons for services provided in respect of the film (other than remuneration paid or payable to or in respect of the persons referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii) or remuneration paid or payable for processing and final preparation of the film) was paid or payable to Canadians,

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: not less than 75 per cent of the aggregate of costs incurred for processing and final preparation of the film including laboratory work, sound recording, sound editing and picture editing (other than remuneration paid or payable to or in respect of persons referred to in subparagraphs (i), (ii) and (iii)), was incurred in respect of services rendered in Canada, and

Subparagraph.Label: (v)
Subparagraph.Text: the copyright protecting its use in Canada is beneficially owned

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: by a person who is either a Canadian or a corporation incorporated under the laws of Canada or a province, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: jointly or otherwise by two or more persons described in clause (A),

ContinuedDefinition.Text: other than a film

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: acquired after the day that is the earlier of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the day of its first commercial use, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: 12 months after the day the principal photography thereof is completed, or

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of which certification under this definition has been revoked by the Minister of Communications as provided in paragraph (10)(b); (long métrage portant visa)

Definition.Text: certified production, in respect of a particular taxation year, means a motion picture film or video tape certified by the Minister of Communications to be a film or tape in respect of which all photography, taping or art work required specifically for the production thereof and all film or tape editing therefor were commenced after May 25, 1976, certified by him to be a film or tape in respect of which the principal photography or taping thereof was commenced before the end of the particular taxation year or was completed no later than 60 days after the end of that year and certified by him to be

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a film or tape the production of which is contemplated in a coproduction agreement entered into between Canada and another country, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a film or tape in respect of which

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the individual who performed the duties of producer was a Canadian,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the Minister of Communications has allotted not less than an aggregate of six units of production, not less than two of which were allotted by virtue of clause (A) or (B) and not less than one of which was allotted by virtue of clause (C) or (D), for individuals who provided services in respect of the film or tape, in the following manner:

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: for the director, two units of production,

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: for the screenwriter, two units of production,

Clause.Label: (C)
Clause.Text: for the actor or actress in respect of whose services for the film or tape the highest remuneration was paid or payable (unless in the opinion of the Minister of Communications the individual did not perform a major role in the film or tape), one unit of production,

Clause.Label: (D)
Clause.Text: for the actor or actress in respect of whose services for the film or tape the second highest remuneration was paid or payable (unless in the opinion of the Minister of Communications the individual did not perform a major role in the film or tape), one unit of production,

Clause.Label: (E)
Clause.Text: for the art director, one unit of production,

Clause.Label: (F)
Clause.Text: for the director of photography, one unit of production,

Clause.Label: (G)
Clause.Text: for the music composer, one unit of production, and

Clause.Label: (H)
Clause.Text: for the picture editor, one unit of production,

ContinuedSubparagraph.Text: shall be allotted, provided the individual in respect of such allotment was a Canadian,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: not less than 75 per cent of the aggregate of all costs (other than costs determined by reference to the amount of income from the film or tape) paid or payable to persons for services provided in respect of producing the film or tape (other than remuneration paid or payable to, or in respect of, individuals referred to in subparagraph (i) or (ii), costs referred to in subparagraph (iv) incurred for processing and final preparation of the film or tape, and amounts paid or payable in respect of insurance, financing, brokerage, legal and accounting fees and similar amounts) was paid or payable to, or in respect of services provided by, Canadians, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: not less than 75 per cent of the aggregate of all costs (other than costs determined by reference to the amount of income from the film or tape) incurred for processing and final preparation of the film or tape, including laboratory work, sound re-recording, sound editing and picture editing (other than remuneration paid or payable to, or in respect of, individuals referred to in subparagraph (i) or (ii)) was incurred in respect of services provided in Canada,

ContinuedDefinition.Text: other than a film or tape

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: acquired after the day that is the earlier of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the day of its first commercial use, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: 12 months after the day the principal photography or taping thereof is completed,

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: acquired by a taxpayer who has not paid in cash, as of the end of the particular taxation year, to the person from whom he acquired the film or tape, at least 5 per cent of the capital cost to the taxpayer of the film or tape as of the end of the year,

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: acquired by a taxpayer who has issued in payment or part payment thereof, a bond, debenture, bill, note, mortgage or similar obligation in respect of which an amount is not due until a time that is more than four years after the end of the taxation year in which the taxpayer acquired the film or tape,

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: acquired from a non-resident, or

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of which certification under this definition has been revoked by the Minister of Communications as provided in paragraph (10)(b),

ContinuedDefinition.Text: and, for the purposes of the application of this definition,

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of a film or tape acquired in 1987, other than a film or tape in respect of which paragraph (i) applies, the reference in this definition to “commenced before the end of the particular taxation year or was completed no later than 60 days after the end of that year” shall be read as a reference to “commenced before the end of 1987 or was completed before July, 1988”; and

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of a film or tape acquired in 1987 or 1988 that is included in paragraph (n) of Class 12 in Schedule II and that is part of a series of films or tapes that includes another property included in that paragraph, the reference in this definition to “commenced before the end of the particular taxation year or was completed no later than 60 days after the end of that year” shall be read as a reference to “completed before 1989”; (production portant visa)

Definition.Text: completion of a specified development phase of a taxpayer’s oil sands project means the first attainment of a level of average output, attributable to the specified development phase and measured over a sixty day period, equal to at least 60% of the planned level of average daily output (as determined in paragraph (b) of the definition specified development phase) in respect of that phase; (achèvement)
computer software includes systems software and a right or licence to use computer software; (logiciel)

data network infrastructure equipment means network infrastructure equipment that controls, transfers, modulates or directs data, and that operates in support of telecommunications applications such as e-mail, instant messaging, audio- and video-over-Internet Protocol or Web browsing, Web searching and Web hosting, including data switches, multiplexers, routers, remote access servers, hubs, domain name servers, and modems, but does not include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: network equipment (other than radio network equipment) that operates in support of telecommunications applications, if the bandwidth made available by that equipment to a single end-user of the network is 64 kilobits per second or less in either direction,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: radio network equipment that operates in support of wireless telecommunications applications unless the equipment supports digital transmission on a radio channel,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: network equipment that operates in support of broadcast telecommunications applications and that is unidirectional,

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: network equipment that is end-user equipment, including telephone sets, personal digital assistants and facsimile transmission devices,

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: equipment that is described in paragraph (f.2) or (v) of Class 10, or in any of Classes 45, 50 and 52, in Schedule II,

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: wires or cables, or similar property, and

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: structures; (matériel d’infrastructure pour réseaux de données)

Definition.Text: designated asset in respect of a development phase of a taxpayer’s oil sands project, means a property that is a building, a structure, machinery or equipment and is, or is an integral and substantial part of,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a bitumen development phase,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: a crusher,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a froth treatment plant,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: a primary separation unit,

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: a steam generation plant,

Subparagraph.Label: (v)
Subparagraph.Text: a cogeneration plant, or

Subparagraph.Label: (vi)
Subparagraph.Text: a water treatment plant, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of an upgrading development phase,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: a gasifier unit,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a vacuum distillation unit,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: a hydrocracker unit,

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: a hydrotreater unit,

Subparagraph.Label: (v)
Subparagraph.Text: a hydroprocessor unit, or

Subparagraph.Label: (vi)
Subparagraph.Text: a coker; (bien désigné)

Definition.Text: designated overburden removal cost of a taxpayer means any cost incurred by him in respect of clearing or removing overburden from a mine in Canada owned or operated by him where the cost

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: was incurred after November 16, 1978 and before 1988,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: was incurred after the mine came into production in reasonable commercial quantities,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: as of the end of the taxation year in which the cost was incurred, has not been deducted by the taxpayer in computing his income, and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: is not deductible, in whole or in part, by the taxpayer in computing his income for a taxation year subsequent to the taxation year in which the cost was incurred, other than by virtue of paragraph 20(1)(a) of the Act; (coût désigné d’enlèvement des terrains de couverture)

Definition.Text: designated underground storage cost of a taxpayer means any cost incurred by him after December 11, 1979 in respect of developing a well, mine or other similar underground property for the storage in Canada of petroleum, natural gas or other related hydrocarbons; (coût désigné de stockage souterrain)

development phase of a taxpayer’s oil sands project means the acquisition, construction, fabrication or installation of a group of assets, by or on behalf of the taxpayer, that may reasonably be considered to constitute a discrete expansion in the capacity of the oil sands project when complete (including, for greater certainty, the initiation of a new oil sands project); (phase de mise en valeur)
eligible greenhouse means a property of a taxpayer that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is located in Canada,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: is acquired by the taxpayer after November 3, 2025,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: is included in

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: Class 6 in Schedule II because of paragraph (d) of that Class, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: Class 8 in Schedule II because of paragraph (m) of that Class, and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: meets either of the following conditions:

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the property is not a property in respect of which an amount has been deducted under paragraph 20(1)(a) or subsection 20(16) of the Act by any person or partnership for a taxation year ending before the time the property was acquired by the taxpayer, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the property was not

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: acquired in circumstances where

Subclause.Label: (I)
Subclause.Text: the taxpayer was deemed to have been allowed or deducted an amount under paragraph 20(1)(a) of the Act in respect of the property in computing income for previous taxation years, or

Subclause.Label: (II)
Subclause.Text: the undepreciated capital cost of depreciable property of a prescribed class of the taxpayer was reduced by an amount determined by reference to the amount by which the capital cost of the property to the taxpayer exceeds its cost amount, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: previously owned or acquired by the taxpayer or by a person or partnership with which the taxpayer did not deal at arm’s length at any time when the property was owned or acquired by the person or partnership; (serre admissible)

Definition.Text: eligible liquefaction building of a taxpayer, in respect of an eligible liquefaction facility of the taxpayer, means property (other than property that has been used or acquired for use for any purpose before it was acquired by the taxpayer or a residential building ) acquired by the taxpayer after February 19, 2015 and before 2025 that is included in Class 1 in Schedule II because of paragraph (q) of that Class and that is used as part of the eligible liquefaction facility; (bâtiment de liquéfaction admissible)
eligible liquefaction equipment in respect of an eligible liquefaction facility of a taxpayer, means property of the taxpayer that is used in connection with the liquefaction of natural gas and that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is acquired by the taxpayer after February 19, 2015 and before 2025,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: is included in Class 47 in Schedule II because of paragraph (b) of that Class,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: has not been used or acquired for use for any purpose before it was acquired by the taxpayer,

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: is not excluded equipment, and

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: is used as part of the eligible liquefaction facility; (matériel de liquéfaction admissible)

Definition.Text: eligible liquefaction facility of a taxpayer means a self-contained system located in Canada — including buildings, structures and equipment — that is used or intended to be used by the taxpayer for the purpose of liquefying natural gas; (installation de liquéfaction admissible)
eligible mine development property means a property acquired by a taxpayer after March 20, 2013 and before 2018 for the purpose of gaining or producing income

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: from a new mine or an expansion of a mine, if the property was acquired under a written agreement entered into by the taxpayer before March 21, 2013,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: from a new mine, if

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the construction of the new mine was started by, or on behalf of, the taxpayer before March 21, 2013 (and for this purpose construction does not include obtaining permits or regulatory approvals, conducting environmental assessments, community consultations or impact benefit studies, and similar activities), or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the engineering and design work for the construction of the new mine, as evidenced in writing, was started by, or on behalf of, the taxpayer before March 21, 2013 (and for this purpose engineering and design work does not include obtaining permits or regulatory approvals, conducting environmental assessments, community consultations or impact benefit studies, and similar activities), or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: from an expansion of a mine, if

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the construction for the expansion of the mine was started by, or on behalf of, the taxpayer before March 21, 2013 (and for this purpose construction does not include obtaining permits or regulatory approvals, conducting environmental assessments, community consultations or impact benefit studies, and similar activities), or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the engineering and design work for the construction of the expansion of the mine, as evidenced in writing, was started by, or on behalf of, the taxpayer before March 21, 2013 (and for this purpose engineering and design work does not include obtaining permits or regulatory approvals, conducting environmental assessments, community consultations or impact benefit studies, and similar activities); (bien admissible à l’aménagement d’une mine)

Definition.Text: eligible non-residential building means a taxpayer’s building (other than a building that was used, or acquired for use, by any person or partnership before March 19, 2007) that is located in Canada, that is included in Class 1 in Schedule II and that is acquired by the taxpayer on or after March 19, 2007 to be used by the taxpayer, or a lessee of the taxpayer, for a non-residential use; (bâtiment non résidentiel admissible)
excluded equipment means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: pipelines (other than pipelines used to move natural gas, or its components that are extracted, within an eligible liquefaction facility during the liquefaction process or used to move liquefied natural gas),

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: equipment used exclusively to regasify liquefied natural gas, and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: electrical generation equipment; (matériel non admissible)

Definition.Text: gas or oil well equipment includes

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: equipment, structures and pipelines, other than a well casing, acquired to be used in a gas or oil field in the production therefrom of natural gas or crude oil, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a pipeline acquired to be used solely for transmitting gas to a natural gas processing plant,

ContinuedDefinition.Text: but does not include

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: equipment or structures acquired for the refining of oil or the processing of natural gas including the separation therefrom of liquid hydrocarbons, sulphur or other joint products or by-products, or

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a pipeline for removal or for collection for immediate removal of natural gas or crude oil from a gas or oil field except a pipeline referred to in paragraph (b); (matériel de puits de gaz ou de pétrole)

Definition.Text: general-purpose electronic data processing equipment means electronic equipment that, in its operation, requires an internally stored computer program that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is executed by the equipment,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: can be altered by the user of the equipment,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: instructs the equipment to read and select, alter or store data from an external medium such as a card, disk or tape, and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: depends upon the characteristics of the data being processed to determine the sequence of its execution; (matériel électronique universel de traitement de l’information)

Definition.Text: new purpose-built residential rental means a purpose-built residential rental that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: was

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: built for use as a purpose-built residential rental if construction began after April 15, 2024 and before 2031, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: previously a building, or part of a building, used as a commercial property that was substantially renovated for use as a purpose-built residential rental if the renovations began after April 15, 2024 and before 2031, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: becomes available for use before 2036; (nouvel ensemble résidentiel construit spécialement pour la location)

Definition.Text: oil sands project of a taxpayer means an undertaking by the taxpayer for the extraction of tar sands from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer, which undertaking may include the processing of the tar sands to a stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent; (projet de sables bitumineux)
oil sands property of a taxpayer means property acquired by the taxpayer for the purpose of earning income from an oil sands project of the taxpayer; (bien de sables bitumineux)
ore includes ore from a mineral resource that has been processed to any stage that is prior to the prime metal stage or its equivalent; (minerai)

preliminary work activity means activity that is preliminary to the acquisition, construction, fabrication or installation by or on behalf of a taxpayer of designated assets in respect of the taxpayer’s oil sands project including, without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the following activities:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: obtaining permits or regulatory approvals,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: performing design or engineering work,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: conducting feasibility studies,

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: conducting environmental assessments,

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: clearing or excavating land,

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: building roads, and

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: entering into contracts; (travaux préliminaires)

Definition.Text: purpose-built residential rental means a building or a part of a building situated in Canada

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: that contains

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: four or more residential rental units at least four of which contain private kitchen facilities, a private bath and a private living area, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: 10 or more residential rental units, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in which all or substantially all the residential rental units are rented or offered for rent for continuous periods of not less than 28 consecutive days; (ensemble résidentiel construit spécialement pour la location)

Definition.Text: railway system includes a railway owned or operated by a common carrier, together with all buildings, rolling stock, equipment and other properties pertaining thereto, but does not include a tramway; (réseau de chemin de fer)
residential rental unit means a housing unit used or intended for use as a rented residential premises that is not provided to the travelling or vacationing public; (logement locatif)

specified development phase of a taxpayer’s oil sands project means a bitumen development phase or an upgrading development phase of the oil sands project which can reasonably be expected to result in a planned level of average daily output (where that output is bitumen or a similar product in the case of a bitumen development phase, or synthetic crude oil or a similar product in the case of an upgrading development phase), and in respect of which phase,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: not including any preliminary work activity, one or more designated assets was, before March 19, 2007,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: acquired by the taxpayer, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: in the process of being constructed, fabricated or installed, by or on behalf of the taxpayer, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the planned level of average daily output is the lesser of,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the level that was the demonstrated intention of the taxpayer as of March 19, 2007 to produce from the specified development phase, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the maximum level of output associated with the design capacity, as of March 19, 2007, of the designated asset referred to in paragraph (a); (phase de mise en valeur déterminée)

Definition.Text: specified oil sands property of a taxpayer means oil sands property, acquired by the taxpayer before 2012, the taxpayer’s use of which is reasonably required

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: for a specified development phase of an oil sands project of the taxpayer to reach completion; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: as part of a bitumen development phase of an oil sands project of the taxpayer,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: to the extent that the output from the bitumen development phase is required for an upgrading development phase that is a specified development phase of the oil sands project to reach completion, and it is reasonable to conclude that all or substantially all of the output from the bitumen development phase will be so used; and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: where it was the demonstrated intention of the taxpayer as of March 19, 2007 to produce, from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer, the bitumen feedstock required for the upgrading development phase to reach completion; (bien de sables bitumineux déterminé)

Definition.Text: specified temporary access road means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a temporary access road to an oil or gas well in Canada, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a temporary access road the cost of which would, if the definition Canadian exploration expense in subsection 66.1(6) of the Act were read without reference to paragraphs (k.1) and (l) of that definition, be a Canadian exploration expense because of paragraph (f) or (g) of that definition; (route d’accès temporaire déterminée)

Definition.Text: systems software means a combination of computer programs and associated procedures, related technical documentation and data that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: performs compilation, assembly, mapping, management or processing of other programs,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: facilitates the functioning of a computer system by other programs,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: provides service or utility functions such as media conversion, sorting, merging, system accounting, performance measurement, system diagnostics or programming aids,

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: provides general support functions such as data management, report generation or security control, or

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: provides general capability to meet widespread categories of problem solving or processing requirements where the specific attributes of the work to be performed are introduced mainly in the form of parameters, constants or descriptors rather than in program logic,

ContinuedDefinition.Text: and includes a right or licence to use such a combination of computer programs and associated procedures, related technical documentation and data; (logiciel d’exploitation)

Definition.Text: tar sands ore means ore extracted from a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales; (minerai de sables asphaltiques)
telegraph system includes the buildings, structures, general plant and communication and other equipment pertaining thereto; (réseau de télégraphe)
telephone system includes the buildings, structures, general plant and communication and other equipment pertaining thereto; (réseau de téléphone)
television commercial message means a commercial message as defined in the Television Broadcasting Regulations, 1987 made under the Broadcasting Act; (message publicitaire pour la télévision)

tramway or trolley bus system includes the buildings, structures, rolling stock, general plant and equipment pertaining thereto and where buses other than trolley buses are operated in connection therewith includes the properties pertaining to those bus operations; (réseau de tramway ou d’autobus à trolley)

upgrading development phase of a taxpayer’s oil sands project means a development phase that expands the oil sands project’s capacity to process bitumen or a similar feedstock (all or substantially all of which is from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer) to the crude oil stage or its equivalent. (phase de valorisation)

Subsection.Text: Except as otherwise provided in subsection (6), in this Part and in Schedules II and V,

Definition.Text: industrial mineral mine includes a peat bog or deposit of peat but does not include a mineral resource; (mine de minéral industriel)
mineral includes peat; (minéral)
mining includes the harvesting of peat. (exploitation minière)

Subsection.Text: The following definitions apply in this Part and Schedules II to VI.

Definition.Text: designated immediate expensing property for a taxation year, means property of an eligible person or partnership that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is immediate expensing property of the eligible person or partnership;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: became available for use by the eligible person or partnership in the taxation year; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: is designated as designated immediate expensing property in prescribed form filed by the eligible person or partnership with the Minister for the taxation year

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: if the eligible person or partnership is a partnership, on or before the day that is 12 months after the day on which any member of the partnership is required to file an information return under section 229 for the fiscal period to which the designation relates, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: in any other case, on or before the day that is 12 months after the eligible person or partnership’s filing-due date for the taxation year to which the designation relates. (bien relatif à la passation en charges immédiate désigné)

Definition.Text: eligible person or partnership for a taxation year, means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a corporation that was a Canadian-controlled private corporation throughout the year;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: an individual (other than a trust) who was resident in Canada throughout the year; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a Canadian partnership all of the members of which were, throughout the period, persons described in paragraph (a) or (b). (personne ou société de personnes admissible)

Definition.Text: immediate expensing property for a taxation year, means property of a prescribed class (other than property included in any of Classes 1 to 6, 14.1, 17, 47, 49 and 51 in Schedule II) of an eligible person or partnership that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is acquired by the eligible person or partnership

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: if the eligible person or partnership is a Canadian-controlled private corporation, after April 18, 2021, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: if the eligible person or partnership is an individual or a Canadian partnership, after December 31, 2021;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: becomes available for use

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: if the eligible person or partnership is an individual or a Canadian partnership all the members of which are individuals throughout the taxation year, before 2025, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: in any other case, before 2024; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: meets either of the following conditions:

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the property

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: has not been used for any purpose before it was acquired by the eligible person or partnership, and

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: is not a property in respect of which an amount has been deducted under paragraph 20(1)(a) or subsection 20(16) of the Act by any person or partnership for a taxation year ending before the time the property was acquired by the eligible person or partnership, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the property was not

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: acquired in circumstances where

Subclause.Label: (I)
Subclause.Text: the eligible person or partnership was deemed to have been allowed or deducted an amount under paragraph 20(1)(a) of the Act in respect of the property in computing income for previous taxation years, or

Subclause.Label: (II)
Subclause.Text: the undepreciated capital cost of depreciable property of a prescribed class of the eligible person or partnership was reduced by an amount determined by reference to the amount by which the capital cost of the property to the eligible person or partnership exceeds its cost amount, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: previously owned or acquired by the eligible person or partnership or by a person or partnership with which the eligible person or partnership did not deal at arm’s length at any time when the property was owned or acquired by the person or partnership. (bien relatif à la passation en charges immédiate)

Definition.Text: taxpayer unless the context otherwise requires, includes an eligible person or partnership. (contribuable)

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this Part and Schedules II to VI, an eligible person or partnership’s immediate expensing limit for a taxation year is $1,500,000 unless the eligible person or partnership is associated (within the meaning of section 256 of the Act, as modified by subsection (3.6)) in the taxation year with one or more other eligible persons or partnerships, in which case, except as otherwise provided in this section, its immediate expensing limit is nil.

Despite subsection (3.2), if all the eligible persons or partnerships that are associated with each other (within the meaning of section 256 of the Act, as modified by subsection (3.6)) in a taxation year file with the Minister in prescribed form an agreement that assigns for the purpose of this Part and Schedules II to VI a percentage to one or more of them for the year, the immediate expensing limit for the year of each of the eligible persons or partnerships is

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the total of the percentages assigned in the agreement does not exceed 100%, $1,500,000 multiplied by the percentage assigned to that eligible person or partnership in the agreement; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in any other case, nil.

Subsection.Text: If any of the eligible persons or partnerships that are associated with each other (within the meaning of section 256 of the Act, as modified by subsection (3.6)) in a taxation year has failed to file with the Minister an agreement described in subsection (3.3) within 30 days after notice in writing by the Minister has been forwarded to any of them that such an agreement is required for the purpose of any assessment of tax under Part I of the Act, the Minister shall, for the purpose of this Part and Schedules II to VI, allocate an amount to one or more of them for the taxation year.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Special rules for immediate expensing limit
Subsection.Text: Despite subsections (3.2) to (3.4),

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: where an eligible person or partnership (in this paragraph referred to as the “first person”) has more than one taxation year ending in the same calendar year and it is associated (within the meaning of section 256 of the Act, as modified by subsection (3.6)) in two or more of those taxation years with another eligible person or partnership (in this paragraph referred to as the “other person”) that has a taxation year ending in that calendar year, the immediate expensing limit of the first person for each taxation year ending in the calendar year in which it is associated (within the meaning of section 256 of the Act, as modified by subsection (3.6)) with the other person that ends after the first such taxation year ending in that calendar year is, subject to the application of paragraph (b), an amount equal to the lesser of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: its immediate expensing limit determined under subsection (3.3) or (3.4) for the first such taxation year ending in the calendar year, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: its immediate expensing limit determined under subsection (3.3) or (3.4) for the particular taxation year ending in the calendar year; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: where an eligible person or partnership has a taxation year that is less than 51 weeks, its immediate expensing limit for the year is that proportion of its immediate expensing limit for the year determined without reference to this paragraph that the number of days in the year is of 365.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this Part and Schedules II to VI, in determining whether an eligible person or partnership is associated (within the meaning of section 256 of the Act, as modified by this subsection) with another eligible person or partnership in a taxation year

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the eligible person or partnership is a partnership,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the partnership is deemed to be a corporation (in this subsection referred to as a “deemed corporation”) for the year,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the deemed corporation is deemed to have a capital stock of a single class of shares, with a total of 100 issued and outstanding shares,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: each member (in this subsection referred to as a “deemed shareholder”) of the deemed corporation is deemed to be a shareholder of the deemed corporation,

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: each deemed shareholder of the deemed corporation is deemed to hold a number of shares in the capital stock of the deemed corporation determined by the formula

FormulaDefinition.Text: is equal to

FormulaParagraph.Label: (A)
FormulaParagraph.Text: the deemed shareholder’s specified proportion for the last fiscal period of the deemed corporation, or

FormulaParagraph.Label: (B)
FormulaParagraph.Text: if the deemed shareholder does not have a specified proportion described in clause (A), the proportion that the fair market value of the deemed shareholder’s interest in the deemed corporation at that time is of the fair market value of all interests in the deemed corporation at that time, and

Subparagraph.Label: (v)
Subparagraph.Text: the deemed corporation’s fiscal period is deemed to be its taxation year; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the eligible person or partnership is an individual (other than a trust) who carries on a business or has acquired immediate expensing property

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the individual, in respect of that business or property, is deemed to be a corporation that is controlled by the individual, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the corporation’s taxation year is deemed to be the same as the individual’s taxation year.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this Part and Schedules II to VI, accelerated investment incentive property means property of a taxpayer (other than property included in any of Classes 54 to 56) that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is acquired by the taxpayer after November 20, 2018 and before 2025 and becomes available for use before 2028; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: meets either of the following conditions:

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the property is not a property in respect of which an amount has been deducted under paragraph 20(1)(a) or subsection 20(16) of the Act by any person or partnership for a taxation year ending before the time the property was acquired by the taxpayer, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the property was not

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: acquired in circumstances where

Subclause.Label: (I)
Subclause.Text: the taxpayer was deemed to have been allowed or deducted an amount under paragraph 20(1)(a) of the Act in respect of the property in computing income for previous taxation years, or

Subclause.Label: (II)
Subclause.Text: the undepreciated capital cost of depreciable property of a prescribed class of the taxpayer was reduced by an amount determined by reference to the amount by which the capital cost of the property to the taxpayer exceeds its cost amount, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: previously owned or acquired by the taxpayer or by a person or partnership with which the taxpayer did not deal at arm’s length at any time when the property was owned or acquired by the person or partnership.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Definition of reaccelerated investment incentive property
Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this Part and Schedules II to VI, reaccelerated investment incentive property means property of a taxpayer (other than property included in any of Classes 54 to 56) that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is acquired by the taxpayer after 2024 and becomes available for use before 2034; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: meets either of the following conditions:

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the property is not a property in respect of which an amount has been deducted under paragraph 20(1)(a) or subsection 20(16) of the Act by any person or partnership for a taxation year ending before the time the property was acquired by the taxpayer, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the property was not

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: acquired in circumstances where

Subclause.Label: (I)
Subclause.Text: the taxpayer was deemed to have been allowed or deducted an amount under paragraph 20(1)(a) of the Act in respect of the property in computing income for previous taxation years, or

Subclause.Label: (II)
Subclause.Text: the undepreciated capital cost of depreciable property of a prescribed class of the taxpayer was reduced by an amount determined by reference to the amount by which the capital cost of the property to the taxpayer exceeds its cost amount, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: previously owned or acquired by the taxpayer or by a person or partnership with which the taxpayer did not deal at arm’s length at any time when the property was owned or acquired by the person or partnership.

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of subparagraph (4)(b)(i), if the capital cost to a taxpayer of a depreciable property (referred to in this subsection as the “single property”) includes amounts incurred at different times, then amounts deducted under paragraph 20(1)(a) or subsection 20(16) of the Act in respect of the single property are deemed to have been deducted in respect of a separate property that is not part of the single property to the extent the deducted amounts can reasonably be considered to be in respect of amounts

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: incurred before November 21, 2018; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: incurred after November 20, 2018, if any portion of the single property is considered to have become available for use before the time the single property is first used for the purpose of earning income.

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of subparagraph (4.01)(b)(i), if the capital cost to a taxpayer of a depreciable property (referred to in this subsection as the “single property”) includes amounts incurred at different times, then amounts deducted under paragraph 20(1)(a) or subsection 20(16) of the Act in respect of the single property are deemed to have been deducted in respect of a separate property that is not part of the single property to the extent the deducted amounts can reasonably be considered to be in respect of amounts

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: incurred before 2025; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: incurred after 2024, if any portion of the single property is considered to have become available for use before the time the single property is first used for the purpose of earning income.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of paragraphs 1100(1)(w) to (ya.2), subsections 1101(4a) to (4h) and Classes 10, 28 and 41 to 41.2 of Schedule II, a taxpayer’s income from a mine, or any expression referring to a taxpayer’s income from a mine, includes income reasonably attributable to

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the processing by the taxpayer of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: ore (other than iron ore or tar sands ore) all or substantially all of which is from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer to any stage that is not beyond the prime metal stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: iron ore all or substantially all of which is from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer to any stage that is not beyond the pellet stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: tar sands ore all or substantially all of which is from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: material extracted by a well, all or substantially all of which is from a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales owned by the taxpayer, to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the production by the taxpayer of material from a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the transportation by the taxpayer of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: output, other than iron ore or tar sands ore, from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer that has been processed by him to any stage that is not beyond the prime metal stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: iron ore from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer that has been processed by him to any stage that is not beyond the pellet stage or its equivalent, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: tar sands ore from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer that has been processed by him to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent,

ContinuedParagraph.Text: to the extent that such transportation is effected through the use of property of the taxpayer that is included in Class 10 in Schedule II because of paragraph (m) thereof or that would be so included if that paragraph were read without reference to subparagraph (v) thereof and if Class 41 in Schedule II were read without the reference therein to that paragraph.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of Classes 41 to 41.2 of Schedule II, a taxpayer’s gross revenue from a mine includes

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: revenue reasonably attributable to the processing by the taxpayer of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: ore (other than iron ore or tar sands ore) from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer to any stage that is not beyond the prime metal stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: iron ore from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer to any stage that is not beyond the pellet stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: tar sands ore from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: material extracted by a well from a mineral resource owned by the taxpayer that is a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the amount, if any, by which any revenue reasonably attributable to the processing by the taxpayer of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: ore (other than iron ore or tar sands ore) from a mineral resource not owned by the taxpayer, to any stage that is not beyond the prime metal stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: iron ore from a mineral resource not owned by the taxpayer to any stage that is not beyond the pellet stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: tar sands ore from a mineral resource not owned by the taxpayer to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: material extracted by a well from a mineral resource not owned by the taxpayer that is a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent

ContinuedParagraph.Text: exceeds the cost to the taxpayer of the ore or material processed; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: revenue reasonably attributable to the production by the taxpayer of material from a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales.

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of subsection (5.1), gross revenue from a mine does not include revenue reasonably attributable to the addition of diluent, for the purpose of transportation, to material extracted from a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales.
For the purposes of Class 10 in Schedule II,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: income from a mine includes income reasonably attributable to the processing of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: ore, other than iron ore or tar sands ore, from a mineral resource not owned by the taxpayer to any stage that is not beyond the prime metal stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: iron ore from a mineral resource not owned by the taxpayer to any stage that is not beyond the pellet stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: tar sands ore from a mineral resource not owned by the taxpayer to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: material extracted by a well from a mineral resource not owned by the taxpayer that is a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: mine includes a well for the extraction of material from a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales or from a deposit of calcium chloride, halite or sylvite.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of paragraphs 1100(1)(w) to (ya.2), subsections 1101(4a) to (4h) and 1102(8) and (9), section 1107 and Classes 12, 28 and 41 to 41.2 of Schedule II,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: mine includes

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: a well for the extraction of material from a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales or from a deposit of calcium chloride, halite or sylvite, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a pit for the extraction of kaolin or tar sands ore,

ContinuedParagraph.Text: but does not include

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: an oil or gas well, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: a sand pit, gravel pit, clay pit, shale pit, peat bog, deposit of peat or a stone quarry (other than a kaolin pit or a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales);

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: all wells of a taxpayer for the extraction of material from one or more deposits of calcium chloride, halite or sylvite, the material produced from which is sent to the same plant for processing, are deemed to be one mine of the taxpayer; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: all wells of a taxpayer for the extraction of material from a deposit of bituminous sands or oil shales that the Minister, in consultation with the Minister of Natural Resources, determines constitute one project, are deemed to be one mine of the taxpayer.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of subsection (7), stone quarry includes a mine producing dimension stone or crushed rock for use as aggregates or for other construction purposes.
For greater certainty, for the purposes of paragraphs (c) and (e) of Class 28 and paragraph (a) of Classes 41 to 41.2 in Schedule II, production means production in reasonable commercial quantities.
For the purposes of paragraph 1100(1)(a.1), subsection 1100(26) and Class 29 in Schedule II, manufacturing or processing does not include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: farming or fishing;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: logging;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: construction;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: operating an oil or gas well or extracting petroleum or natural gas from a natural accumulation thereof;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: extracting minerals from a mineral resource;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: processing of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: ore, other than iron ore or tar sands ore, from a mineral resource to any stage that is not beyond the prime metal stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: iron ore from a mineral resource to any stage that is not beyond the pellet stage or its equivalent, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: tar sands ore from a mineral resource to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent;

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: producing industrial minerals;

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: producing or processing electrical energy or steam, for sale;

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: processing natural gas as part of the business of selling or distributing gas in the course of operating a public utility;

Paragraph.Label: (j)
Paragraph.Text: processing heavy crude oil recovered from a natural reservoir in Canada to a stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent; or

Paragraph.Label: (k)
Paragraph.Text: Canadian field processing.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of subsection 1100(21) and the definitions certified feature film and certified production and in subsection (2),

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: Canadian means an individual who was, at all relevant times,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: a Canadian citizen as defined in the Citizenship Act, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a permanent resident within the meaning of the Immigration Act, 1976;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a motion picture film or video tape that has been certified by

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the Secretary of State, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the Minister of Communications

ContinuedParagraph.Text: as a certified feature film or certified production, as the case may be, may have its certification revoked by the Minister of Communications where an incorrect statement was made in the furnishing of information for the purpose of obtaining that certification and a certification that has been so revoked is void from the time of its issue;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: remuneration does not include an amount determined by reference to the amount of income from a motion picture film or video tape;

Paragraph.Label: (c.1)
Paragraph.Text: revenue guarantee means a contract or other arrangement under the terms of which a taxpayer has a right to receive a minimum rental revenue or other fixed revenue in respect of a right to the use, in any manner whatever, of a certified feature film or certified production;

Paragraph.Label: (c.2)
Paragraph.Text: a screenwriter shall be deemed to be an individual who is a Canadian where

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: each individual involved in the preparation of the screenplay is a Canadian, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the principal screenwriter is an individual who is a Canadian and

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: the screenplay for the motion picture film or video tape is based upon a work authored by a Canadian,

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: copyright in the work subsists in Canada, and

Clause.Label: (C)
Clause.Text: the work is published in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: unit of production means a measure used by the Minister of Communications in determining the weight to be given for each individual Canadian referred to in subparagraph (b)(ii) of the definition certified production in subsection (2) who provides services in respect of a motion picture film or video tape; and

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: where each individual who performed a service in respect of a motion picture film or video tape as the

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: director,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: screenwriter,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: actor or actress in respect of whose services for the film or tape the highest remuneration was paid or payable,

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: actor or actress in respect of whose services for the film or tape the second highest remuneration was paid or payable,

Subparagraph.Label: (v)
Subparagraph.Text: art director,

Subparagraph.Label: (vi)
Subparagraph.Text: director of photoghraphy,

Subparagraph.Label: (vii)
Subparagraph.Text: music composer, or

Subparagraph.Label: (viii)
Subparagraph.Text: picture editor

ContinuedParagraph.Text: was a Canadian, the Minister of Communications shall be deemed to have allotted six units of production in respect of the film or tape for the purposes of the definition certified production in subsection (2).

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of paragraph (h) of Class 34 in Schedule II, a certificate issued under

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: subparagraph (d)(i) of that class may be revoked by the Minister of Industry, Trade and Commerce, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: subparagraph (d)(ii) or paragraph (g) of that class, as the case may be, may be revoked by the Minister of Energy, Mines and Resources

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: where

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: an incorrect statement was made in the furnishing of information for the purpose of obtaining the certificate, or

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the taxpayer does not conform to the plan described in subparagraph (d)(i) or (d)(ii) of that class, as the case may be,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: and a certificate that has been so revoked shall be void from the time of its issue.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of Class 37 in Schedule II, amusement park means a park open to the public where amusements, rides and audio-visual attractions are permanently situated.

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Subsection.Text: The definitions in this subsection apply for the purposes of this subsection, subsections (14) to (17) and Classes 43.1 and 43.2 in Schedule II.

Definition.Text: basic oxygen furnace gas means the gas that is produced intermittently in a basic oxygen furnace of a steel mill by the chemical reaction of carbon in molten steel and pure oxygen. (gaz de convertisseur basique à oxygène)
biogas means the gas produced by the anaerobic digestion of specified waste material. (biogaz)
bio-oil means liquid fuel that is created from wood waste or plant residues using a thermo-chemical conversion process that takes place in the absence of oxygen. (bio-huile)

blast furnace gas means the gas produced in a blast furnace of a steel mill, by the chemical reaction of carbon (in the form of coke, coal or natural gas), the oxygen in air and iron ore. (gaz de haut fourneau)

digester gas means a mixture of gases that are produced from the decomposition of organic waste in a digester and that are extracted from an eligible sewage treatment facility for that organic waste. (gaz de digesteur)
distribution equipment means equipment (other than transmission equipment) used to distribute electrical energy generated by electrical generating equipment. (matériel de distribution)

district energy equipment means property that is part of a district energy system and that consists of pipes or pumps used to collect and distribute an energy transfer medium, meters, control equipment, chillers and heat exchangers that are attached to the main distribution line of a district energy system, but does not include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: property used to distribute water that is for consumption, disposal or treatment; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: property that is part of the internal heating or cooling system of a building. (équipement de réseau énergétique de quartier)

Definition.Text: district energy system means a system that is used primarily to provide heating or cooling by continuously circulating, from a central generation unit to one or more buildings through a system of interconnected pipes, an energy transfer medium that is heated or cooled using thermal energy. (réseau énergétique de quartier)
eligible electrical generation equipment means property that is electrical generating equipment described in

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: subparagraph (d)(iii.1), (v), (vi), (vii), (xiv) or (xix) of Class 43.1 in Schedule II; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: subparagraph (e)(i) or (iii) of the definition clean electricity property in subsection 127.491(1) of the Act. (matériel générateur d’électricité admissible)

Definition.Text: eligible landfill site means a landfill site that is situated in Canada, or a former landfill site that is situated in Canada, and, if a permit or licence in respect of the site is or was required under any law of Canada or of a province, for which the permit or licence has been issued. (site d’enfouissement admissible)

eligible sewage treatment facility means a sewage treatment facility that is situated in Canada and for which a permit or licence is issued under any law of Canada or of a province. (installation admissible de traitement des eaux usées)
eligible transmission equipment means property (other than a building) that is transmission equipment of a taxpayer where

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the transmission equipment is used in connection with eligible electrical generation equipment of the taxpayer; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: on annual basis

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: more than 75% of the electrical energy generated by the eligible electrical generation equipment is transmitted by the transmission equipment, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: more than 75% of the electrical energy transmitted by the transmission equipment is generated by the eligible electrical generation equipment. (matériel de transmission admissible)

Definition.Text: eligible waste fuel means biogas, bio-oil, digester gas, landfill gas, municipal waste, plant residue, pulp and paper waste and wood waste. (combustible résiduaire admissible)

eligible waste management facility means a waste management facility that is situated in Canada and for which a permit or licence is issued under any law of Canada or of a province. (installation admissible de gestion des déchets)

enhanced combined cycle system means an electrical generating system in which thermal waste from one or more natural gas compressor systems is recovered and used to contribute at least 20 per cent of the energy input of a combined cycle process in order to enhance the generation of electricity, but does not include the natural gas compressor systems. (système à cycles combinés amélioré)
food and animal waste means organic waste that is disposed of in accordance with the laws of Canada or a province and that is

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: generated during the preparation or processing of food or beverage for human or animal consumption;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: food or beverage that is no longer fit for human or animal consumption; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: animal remains. (déchets alimentaires et animaux)

Definition.Text: fossil fuel means a fuel that is petroleum, natural gas or related hydrocarbons, basic oxygen furnace gas, blast furnace gas, coal, coal gas, coke, coke oven gas, lignite or peat. (combustible fossile)

gaseous biofuel means a fuel produced all or substantially all from specified waste material that is a gas at a temperature of 15.6°C (60°F) and a pressure of 101 kPa (14.7 psia). (biocarburants gazeux)
landfill gas means a mixture of gases that are produced from the decomposition of organic waste and that are extracted from an eligible landfill site. (gaz d’enfouissement)

liquid biofuel means a fuel produced all or substantially all from specified waste material or carbon dioxide that is a liquid at a temperature of 15.6°C (60°F) and a pressure of 101 kPa (14.7 psia). (biocarburants liquides)

municipal waste means the combustible portion of waste material (other than waste material that is considered to be toxic or hazardous waste pursuant to any law of Canada or of a province) that is generated in Canada and that is accepted at an eligible landfill site or an eligible waste management facility and that, when burned to generate energy, emits only those fluids or other emissions that are in compliance with the law of Canada or of a province. (déchets municipaux)

plant residue means residue of plants (not including wood waste and waste that no longer has the chemical properties of the plants of which it is a residue) that would otherwise be waste material. (résidus végétaux)
producer gas means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of a property of a taxpayer that becomes available for use by the taxpayer before 2025, fuel the composition of which, excluding its water content, is all or substantially all non-condensable gases that is generated primarily from eligible waste fuel or specified waste material using a thermo-chemical conversion process and that is not generated from any feedstock other than eligible waste fuel, specified waste material or fossil fuel; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of a property of a taxpayer that becomes available for use by the taxpayer after 2024, fuel

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the composition of which, excluding its water content, is all or substantially all non-condensable gases,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: that is generated using a thermo-chemical conversion process,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: that is generated from feedstock of which no more than 25% is fossil fuel when measured in terms of energy content (expressed as a higher heating value of the feedstock), and

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: that is not generated from any feedstock other than eligible waste fuel, specified waste material or fossil fuel. (gaz de gazéification)

Definition.Text: pulp and paper by-product means tall oil soaps and crude tall oil that are produced as by-products of the processing of wood into pulp or paper and the by-product of a pulp or paper plant’s effluent treatment or its de-inking processes. (sous-produit d’usine de pâtes ou papiers)
pulp and paper waste means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: tall oil soaps, crude tall oil and turpentine that are produced as by-products of the processing of wood into pulp or paper; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
