Subclause.Text: an eligible expense within the meaning of the Canadian Exploration Incentive Program Act in respect of which the taxpayer, a partnership of which the taxpayer was a member or a principal-business corporation of which the taxpayer was a shareholder corporation, has received, is entitled to receive or may reasonably be expected to receive at any time an incentive under that Act,

Clause.Label: (C)
Clause.Text: the stated percentage of the capital cost to it of property that is tertiary recovery equipment, and

Clause.Label: (D)
Clause.Text: the stated percentage of the capital cost to it of property that is, or but for Class 41 of Schedule II would be, included in Class 10 in Schedule II by virtue of paragraph (u) of the description of that Class, other than the capital cost to it of property that had, before the property was acquired by it, been used for any purpose whatever by any person with whom it was not dealing at arm’s length,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: all amounts, in respect of expenditures (other than expenditures referred to in paragraph (a) or expenditures to acquire property under circumstances that entitled the taxpayer to a deduction under section 1202 or would so entitle the taxpayer if the amounts referred to in paragraphs 1202(2)(a) and (b) were sufficient for the purpose) incurred by the taxpayer after May 8, 1972 and before the particular time, each of which was the stated percentage of the capital cost to the taxpayer of property that is or, but for Class 41, would be included in Class 10 in Schedule II because of paragraph (k) of the description of that Class and that was acquired for the purpose of processing in Canada

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: ore (other than iron ore or tar sands ore), after its extraction from a mineral resource, to any stage that is not beyond the prime metal stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: iron ore, after its extraction from a mineral resource, to any stage that is not beyond the pellet stage or its equivalent, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: tar sands ore, after its extraction from a mineral resource, to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent,

ContinuedParagraph.Text: other than the capital cost to him of property that had, before the property was acquired by the taxpayer, been used for any purpose whatever by any person with whom the taxpayer was not dealing at arm’s length,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: all amounts, in respect of expenditures (other than expenditures referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) or expenditures to acquire property under circumstances that entitled the taxpayer to a deduction under section 1202 or would so entitle the taxpayer if the amounts referred to in paragraphs 1202(2)(a) and (b) were sufficient for the purpose) incurred by the taxpayer before the particular time, each of which was the stated percentage of the capital cost to the taxpayer of property (other than property that had, before it was acquired by the taxpayer, been used for any purpose whatever by any person with whom the taxpayer was not dealing at arm’s length) that is included in Class 28 or paragraph (a) of Class 41, in Schedule II, other than property so included

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: by virtue of the first reference in Class 28 to paragraph (l) of Class 10 in Schedule II, where the property was acquired by the taxpayer before November 17, 1978,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: by virtue of the reference in Class 28 to paragraph (m) of Class 10 in Schedule II,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: that is bituminous sands equipment acquired by an individual, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: that is bituminous sands equipment acquired by a corporation before 1981,

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: all expenditures (other than expenditures referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c)) each of which was incurred by him before November 8, 1969 relating to a mine that came into production in reasonable commercial quantities before that date and that were incurred for the purpose of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: exploration in respect of, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: development of the mine for the purpose of gaining or producing income from the extraction of material from,

ContinuedParagraph.Text: a bituminous sands deposit, an oil sands deposit or an oil shale deposit,

Paragraph.Label: (d.1)
Paragraph.Text: three times the total of all amounts each of which is an amount equal to the lesser of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount that would be determined under subsection 1210(1) in computing the taxpayer’s income for a taxation year that ends before the particular time, if the amount determined for C under that subsection were nil, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount determined for C under subsection 1210(1) in respect of the taxpayer for that year, and

Paragraph.Label: (d.2)
Paragraph.Text: three times the aggregate of all amounts each of which is the specified amount determined under subsection 1202(4) in respect of the taxpayer for a taxation year ending after February 17, 1987 and before the particular time,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: exceeds the aggregate of

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: all amounts deducted by the taxpayer under section 1201 in computing his income for all taxation years ending after May 6, 1974 and before the particular time;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: 33 1/3 per cent of the aggregate of all amounts, each of which is the stated percentage of a cost of borrowing capital, including any cost incurred prior to the commencement of carrying on a business, that was

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: included in the capital cost to him of depreciable property described in subparagraph (a)(iv), clause (a)(vi)(C) or (D) or paragraph (b) or (c), or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: an expenditure described in paragraph (d);

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: 33 1/3 per cent of the aggregate of all amounts, each of which is an amount

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: that became receivable by the taxpayer after April 28, 1978 and before the earlier of December 12, 1979 and the particular time, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: in respect of which the consideration given by the taxpayer therefor was a property (other than a share, or a property that would have been a Canadian resource property if it had been acquired by the taxpayer at the time the consideration was given) or services, the cost of which may reasonably be regarded as having been primarily an expenditure that was added in computing

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: the taxpayer’s earned depletion base by reason of subparagraph (a)(i), (ii) or (iii) or paragraph (d), or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: the earned depletion base of an original owner of a property by reason of subparagraph (a)(i), (ii) or (iii) or paragraph (d) as it applied to the original owner, where the taxpayer acquired the property in circumstances in which subsection 1202(2) applies,

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: 33 1/3 per cent of the aggregate of all amounts, each of which is

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: an amount in respect of a disposition of property (other than a disposition of property that had been used by the taxpayer to any person with whom the taxpayer was not dealing at arm’s length) of the taxpayer after April 28, 1978 and before the earlier of December 12, 1979 and the particular time, the capital cost of which was added in computing

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: the taxpayer’s earned depletion base by reason of subparagraph (a)(iv) or paragraph (b) or (c), or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: the earned depletion base of an original owner of a property by reason of subparagraph (a)(iv) or paragraph (b) or (c) as it applied to the original owner, where the taxpayer acquired the property in circumstances in which subsection 1202(2) applies, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: equal to the lesser of

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: the proceeds of disposition of the property, and

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: the capital cost of the property to the taxpayer, where clause (i)(A) applies, or the original owner, where clause (i)(B) applies, computed as if no amount had been included therein that is a cost of borrowing capital, including any cost incurred prior to the commencement of carrying on a business,

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: any amount required by paragraph 1202(2)(b) (as it read in its application to taxation years ending before February 18, 1987) or paragraph 1202(3)(a) to be deducted at or before the particular time in computing the taxpayer’s earned depletion base,

Paragraph.Label: (j)
Paragraph.Text: 33 1/3 per cent of the aggregate of all amounts, each of which is in respect of an amount of assistance or benefit in respect of Canadian exploration expenses or Canadian development expenses or that may reasonably be related to Canadian exploration activities or Canadian development activities, whether such amount is by way of a grant, subsidy, rebate, forgivable loan, deduction from royalty or tax, rebate of royalty or tax, investment allowance or any other form of assistance or benefit that

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the taxpayer before the particular time has received or was entitled to receive, or that the taxpayer at or after the particular time becomes entitled to receive, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: an original owner or predecessor owner of a property before the particular time has received or was entitled to receive, or at or after the particular time becomes entitled to receive, where the original owner or the predecessor owner received, became entitled to receive or becomes entitled to receive that amount

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: at or after the time at which the property was acquired by the taxpayer in circumstances in which subsection 1202(2) applies, and

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: before the time at which the taxpayer becomes a predecessor owner of the property,

ContinuedParagraph.Text: and that is equal to

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: where the assistance or benefit was in respect of an amount added by reason of subparagraph (a)(ii) or clause (a)(vi)(B) or (B.1) in computing

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: the earned depletion base of the taxpayer (other than such portion thereof included in determining an amount described in paragraph 1202(2)(a) before the particular time), or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: the portion of the earned depletion base of the original owner included in determining an amount described in paragraph 1202(2)(a) before the particular time,

ContinuedSubparagraph.Text: the stated percentage of the amount of the assistance or benefit, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: where the assistance or benefit was in respect of an amount of Canadian oil and gas exploration expense added by reason of subparagraph (a)(v) or clause (a)(vi)(A) in computing

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: the earned depletion base of the taxpayer (other than such portion thereof included in determining an amount described in paragraph 1202(2)(a) before the particular time), or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: the portion of the earned depletion base of the original owner included in determining an amount described in paragraph 1202(2)(a) before the particular time,

ContinuedSubparagraph.Text: the amount equal to the product obtained when the amount of the assistance or benefit is multiplied by the specified percentage in respect of the expense for the calendar year in which the taxpayer or the original owner, as the case may be, incurred the expense, and

Paragraph.Label: (k)
Paragraph.Text: the amount, if any, by which

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the aggregate of all amounts that would be determined under paragraphs 1212(3)(d) to (i)

ContinuedParagraph.Text: exceeds

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the aggregate of all amounts that would be determined under paragraphs 1212(3) (a) to (c)

ContinuedParagraph.Text: in computing his supplementary depletion base at the particular time.

Subsection.Text: Where an expense is incurred before the particular time referred to in subsection (1) and a person at or after the particular time becomes entitled to receive an amount of assistance or benefit in respect of the expense, the amount of such assistance or benefit shall be included in “the amount of the assistance or benefit” referred to in subparagraphs (1)(j)(iii) and (iv) as of the particular time.

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Subsection.Text: In this Part,

Definition.Text: bituminous sands equipment means property of a taxpayer that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is included in Class 28 or in paragraph (a) of Class 41 in Schedule II, other than property so included

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: by virtue of the first reference in Class 28 to paragraph (l) of Class 10 in Schedule II, where the property was acquired by the taxpayer before November 17, 1978, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: by virtue of the reference in Class 28 to paragraph (m) of Class 10 in Schedule II, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: was acquired by the taxpayer after April 10, 1978 principally for the purpose of gaining or producing income from one or more mines, each of which is a location in a bituminous sands deposit, oil sands deposit or oil shale deposit from which material is extracted; (matériel d’exploitation de sables bitumineux)

Definition.Text: Canadian exploration and development overhead expense of a taxpayer means a Canadian exploration expense or a Canadian development expense of the taxpayer made or incurred after 1980 that is not a Canadian renewable and conservation expense (in this definition having the meaning assigned by subsection 66.1(6) of the Act) nor a taxpayer’s share of a Canadian renewable and conservation expense incurred by a partnership and

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: that was in respect of the administration, management or financing of the taxpayer,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: that was in respect of the salary, wages or other remuneration or related benefits paid in respect of a person employed by the taxpayer whose duties were not all or substantially all directed towards exploration or development activities,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: that was in respect of the upkeep or maintenance of, taxes or insurance in respect of, or rental or leasing of, property other than property all or substantially all of the use of which by the taxpayer was for the purposes of exploration or development activities, or

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: that may reasonably be regarded as having been in respect of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the use of or the right to use any property in which any person who was connected with the taxpayer had an interest,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: compensation for the performance of a service for the benefit of the taxpayer by any person who was connected with the taxpayer, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: the acquisition of any materials, parts or supplies from any person who was connected with the taxpayer

ContinuedParagraph.Text: to the extent that the expense exceeds the least of amounts, each of which was the aggregate of the costs incurred by a person who was connected with the taxpayer

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: in respect of the property,

Subparagraph.Label: (v)
Subparagraph.Text: in respect of the performance of the service, or

Subparagraph.Label: (vi)
Subparagraph.Text: in respect of the materials, parts or supplies; (frais généraux d’exploration et d’aménagement au Canada)

Definition.Text: Canadian oil and gas exploration expense, of a taxpayer, means an outlay or expense that is made or incurred after 1980 and that would be a Canadian exploration expense, as defined in subsection 66.1(6) of the Act, of the taxpayer (other than an outlay or expense in respect of a qualified tertiary oil recovery project that is a Canadian exploration expense of the taxpayer because of subparagraph (c)(ii) or (d)(ii) of that definition) if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: that definition were read without reference to its paragraphs (f) to (g.4),

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the reference in paragraph (h) of that definition to “any of paragraphs (a) to (d) and (f) to (g.4)” were read as “any of paragraphs (a) to (e)”, and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the reference in paragraph (i) of that definition to “any of paragraphs (a) to (g)” were read as “any of paragraphs (a) to (e)”; (frais d’exploration pétrolière et gazière au Canada)

Definition.Text: coal mine operator means a person who undertakes all or substantially all of the activities involved in the production of coal from a resource; (exploitant de mine de charbon)
conventional lands means lands situated in Canada other than non-conventional lands; (terres conventionnelles)
disposition of property has the meaning assigned by paragraph 13(21)(c) of the Act; (disposition de biens)
enhanced recovery equipment means property of a taxpayer that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is included in Class 10 in Schedule II by virtue of paragraph (j) of the description of that Class, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: was acquired by the taxpayer after April 10, 1978 and before 1981 for use in the production of oil, from a reservoir or a deposit of bituminous sand, oil sand or oil shale in Canada operated by the taxpayer, that is incremental to oil that would be recovered using primary recovery techniques alone,

ContinuedDefinition.Text: other than property

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: used by the taxpayer as part of a primary recovery process prior to the use described in paragraph (b),

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: that had, before it was acquired by the taxpayer, been used for any purpose whatever by any person with whom the taxpayer was not dealing at arm’s length, or

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: that has been used by any person before April 11, 1978 in the production of oil, from a reservoir in Canada, that is incremental to oil that would be recovered using primary recovery techniques alone; (matériel amélioré de récupération)

Definition.Text: exporting resource means, in relation to a particular processing property of a taxpayer, a resource the ore or any portion thereof produced from which during the year immediately preceding the day on which the property was acquired by the taxpayer was ordinarily processed outside Canada to any stage that is not beyond the prime metal stage or its equivalent; (ressource destinée à l’exportation)
mine means any location where material is extracted from a resource but does not include a well for the extraction of material from a deposit of bituminous sand, oil sand or oil shale; (mine)

non-conventional lands means lands that belong to Her Majesty in right of Canada, or in respect of which Her Majesty in right of Canada has the right to dispose of or exploit the natural resources, situated in

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the Yukon Territory, the Northwest Territories or Sable Island, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: those submarine areas, not within a province, adjacent to the coast of Canada and extending throughout the natural prolongation of the land territory of Canada to the outer edge of the continental margin or to a distance of two hundred nautical miles from the baselines from which the breadth of the territorial sea of Canada is measured, whichever is the greater; (terres non conventionnelles)

Definition.Text: ore includes ore from a mineral resource that has been processed to any stage that is prior to the prime metal stage or its equivalent; (minerai)
original owner of a property means a person

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: who owned the property and disposed of it to a corporation that acquired it in circumstances in which subsection 1202(2) applies, or would apply if the corporation had continued to own the property, to the corporation in respect of the property, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: who would, but for paragraph 1202(2)(b) (as it read in its application to taxation years ending before February 18, 1987) or paragraph 1202(3)(a), as the case may be, be entitled in computing the person’s income for a taxation year ending after the person disposed of the property to a deduction under section 1201 in respect of expenditures that were incurred by the person before the person disposed of the property; (propriétaire obligé)

Definition.Text: predecessor owner of a property means a corporation

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: that acquired the property in circumstances in which subsection 1202(2) applies, or would apply if the corporation had continued to own the property, to the corporation in respect of the property,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: that disposed of the property to another corporation that acquired it in circumstances in which subsection 1202(2) applies, or would apply if the other corporation had continued to own the property, to the other corporation in respect of the property, and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: that would, but for subsection 1202(10), be entitled in computing its income for a taxation year after it disposed of the property to a deduction under subsection 1202(2) in respect of expenditures incurred by an original owner of the property; (propriétaire antérieur)

Definition.Text: primary recovery means the recovery of oil from a reservoir as a result of utilizing the natural energy of the reservoir to move the oil toward a producing well; (récupération primaire)
proceeds of disposition of property has the meaning assigned by paragraph 13(21)(d) of the Act; (produit de la disposition)
processing property means property

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: that is included in Class 10 in Schedule II because of paragraph (g) of the description of that Class or would be so included if that paragraph were read without reference to subparagraph (ii) of that paragraph and Schedule II were read without reference to Class 41, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: that is included in Class 10 in Schedule II because of paragraph (k) of the description of that Class or would be so included if that paragraph were read without reference to the words following subparagraph (ii) of that paragraph and Schedule II were read without reference to Class 41,

ContinuedDefinition.Text: other than property that had, before it was acquired by a taxpayer, been used for any purpose whatever by any person with whom the taxpayer was not dealing at arm’s length; (biens servant au traitement)

Definition.Text: qualified resource means, in relation to a particular processing property of a taxpayer, a resource that, within a reasonable time after the property was acquired by him,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: came into production in reasonable commercial quantities, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: was the subject of a major expansion whereby the greatest designed capacity, measured in weight of input of ore, of the mill that processed ore from the resource was not less than 25% greater in the year immediately following the expansion than it was in the year immediately preceding the expansion; (ressource admissible)

Definition.Text: qualified tertiary oil recovery project in respect of an expense incurred in a taxation year means a project that uses a method (including a method that uses carbon dioxide miscible, hydrocarbon miscible, thermal or chemical processes but not including a secondary recovery method) that is designed to recover oil from an oil well in Canada that is incremental to oil that would be recovered therefrom by primary recovery and a secondary recovery method, if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a specified royalty provision applies in the year or in the immediately following taxation year in respect of the production, if any, or any portion thereof from the project or in respect of the ownership of property to which such production relates,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the project is on a reserve within the meaning of the Indian Act, or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the project is located in the Province of Ontario; (projet qualifié de récupération tertiaire du pétrole)

Definition.Text: resource means any mineral resource in Canada; (ressource)
resource activity of a taxpayer means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the production by the taxpayer of petroleum, natural gas or related hydrocarbons or sulphur from

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: an oil or gas well in Canada, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a natural accumulation (other than a mineral resource) of petroleum or natural gas in Canada,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the production and processing in Canada by the taxpayer or the processing in Canada by the taxpayer of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: ore (other than iron ore or tar sands ore) from a mineral resource in Canada to any stage that is not beyond the prime metal stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: iron ore from a mineral resource in Canada to any stage that is not beyond the pellet stage or its equivalent, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: tar sands ore from a mineral resource in Canada to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the processing in Canada by the taxpayer of heavy crude oil recovered from an oil or gas well in Canada to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent,

Paragraph.Label: (c.1)
Paragraph.Text: Canadian field processing carried on by the taxpayer,

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the processing in Canada by the taxpayer of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: ore (other than iron ore or tar sands ore) from a mineral resource outside Canada to any stage that is not beyond the prime metal stage or its equivalent,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: iron ore from a mineral resource outside Canada to any stage that is not beyond the pellet stage or its equivalent, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: tar sands ore from a mineral resource outside Canada to any stage that is not beyond the crude oil stage or its equivalent, or

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: the ownership by the taxpayer of a right to a rental or royalty computed by reference to the amount or value of production from a natural accumulation of petroleum or natural gas in Canada, an oil or gas well in Canada or a mineral resource in Canada,

ContinuedDefinition.Text: and, for the purposes of this definition,

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: the production of a substance by a taxpayer includes exploration and development activities of the taxpayer with respect to the substance, whether or not extraction of the substance has begun or will ever begin,

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: the production or the processing, or the production and processing, of a substance by a taxpayer includes activities performed by the taxpayer that are ancillary to, or in support of, the production or the processing, or the production and processing, of that substance by the taxpayer,

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: the production or processing of a substance by a taxpayer includes an activity (including the ownership of property) that is undertaken before the extraction of the substance and that is undertaken for the purpose of extracting or processing the substance,

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: the production or the processing, or the production and processing, of a substance by a taxpayer includes activities that the taxpayer undertakes as a consequence of the production or the processing, or the production and processing, of that substance, whether or not the production, the processing or the production and processing of the substance has ceased, and

Paragraph.Label: (j)
Paragraph.Text: notwithstanding paragraphs (a) to (i), the production, the processing or the production and processing of a substance does not include any activity of a taxpayer that is part of a source described in paragraph 1204(1)(b), where

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the activity

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: is the transporting, transmitting or processing (other than processing described in subparagraph (b)(iii), paragraph (c) or (c.1) or subparagraph (d)(iii)) of petroleum, natural gas or related hydrocarbons or of sulphur, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: can reasonably be attributed to a service rendered by the taxpayer, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: revenues derived from the activity are not taken into account in computing the taxpayer’s gross resource profits; (activité extractive)

Definition.Text: secondary recovery method means a method to recover from a reservoir oil that is incremental to oil that would be recovered therefrom by primary recovery, by supplying energy to supplement or replace the natural energy of the reservoir through the use of technically proven methods, including waterflooding; (méthode de récupération secondaire)
specified percentage for a calendar year

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of a Canadian oil and gas exploration expense of a taxpayer for that year incurred in respect of conventional lands means,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: for the 1981 calendar year, 100 per cent,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: for the 1982 calendar year, 60 per cent, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: for the 1983 calendar year, 30 per cent, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of a Canadian oil and gas exploration expense of a taxpayer for that year incurred in respect of non-conventional lands means,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: for the 1981 and 1982 calendar years, 100 per cent,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: for the 1983 calendar year, 60 per cent, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: for the 1984 calendar year, 30 per cent; (pourcentage désigné)

Definition.Text: specified property of a person means all or substantially all of the property used by the person in carrying on in Canada such of the businesses described in subparagraphs 66(15)(h)(i) to (vii) of the Act as were carried on by the person; (biens déterminés)
stated percentage means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: where the taxpayer is an individual other than a trust, in respect of subparagraph 1203(2)(a)(i),

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: 100 per cent in respect of an expenditure incurred before 1989,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: 50 per cent in respect of an expenditure incurred after 1988 and before 1990, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: 0 per cent in respect of an expenditure incurred after 1989,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of subparagraph 1203(2)(a)(i) (where paragraph (a) is not applicable) and paragraphs 1205(1)(a), (b), (c) and (f)

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: 100 per cent in respect of an expenditure incurred or a cost incurred in borrowing capital before July 1, 1988,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: 50 per cent in respect of an expenditure incurred or a cost incurred in borrowing capital after June 30, 1988 and before 1990, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: 0 per cent in respect of an expenditure incurred or a cost incurred in borrowing capital after 1989,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: where the taxpayer is an individual other than a trust, in respect of subparagraph 1203(2)(a)(ii) and subsection 1203(4),

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: 100 per cent in respect of any assistance that relates to expenditures incurred before 1989,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: 50 per cent in respect of any assistance that relates to expenditures incurred after 1988 and before 1990, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: 0 per cent in respect of any assistance that relates to expenditures incurred after 1989, and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of subparagraph 1203(2)(a)(ii) (if paragraph (c) is not applicable), subsection 1203(4) (if paragraph (c) is not applicable) and subparagraph 1205(1)(j)(iii),

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: 100 per cent in respect of any assistance or benefit that relates to expenditures incurred before July 1, 1988,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: 50 per cent in respect of any assistance or benefit that relates to expenditures incurred after June 30, 1988 and before 1990, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: 0 per cent in respect of any assistance or benefit that relates to expenditures incurred after 1989; (pourcentage indiqué)

Definition.Text: tar sands ore means ore extracted, other than through a well, from a mineral resource that is a deposit of bituminous sand, oil sand or oil shale; (minerai de sables asphaltiques)
tertiary recovery equipment means property of a taxpayer that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is, or but for Class 41 in Schedule II would be, included in Class 10 in Schedule II by virtue of paragraph (j) of the description of that Class,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: was acquired by the taxpayer after 1980 for use in a qualified tertiary oil recovery project,

ContinuedDefinition.Text: other than property

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: used by the taxpayer for another use prior to the use described in paragraph (b), or

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: that had, before it was acquired by the taxpayer, been used for any purpose whatever by any person with whom the taxpayer was not dealing at arm’s length. (matériel de récupération tertiaire)

Subsection.Text: In this Part, joint exploration corporation, principal-business corporation, production from a Canadian resource property, reserve amount and shareholder corporation have the meanings assigned by subsection 66(15) of the Act.
For the purposes of sections 1201 to 1209 and 1212, where at the end of a fiscal period of a partnership, a taxpayer was a member thereof

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the resource profits of the partnership for the fiscal period, to the extent of the taxpayer’s share thereof, shall be included in computing his resource profits for his taxation year in which the fiscal period ended;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any property acquired or disposed of by the partnership shall be deemed to have been acquired or disposed of by the taxpayer to the extent of his share of thereof;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: any property deemed by paragraph (b) to have been acquired or disposed of by the taxpayer shall be deemed to have been acquired or disposed of by him on the day the property was acquired or disposed of by the partnership;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: any amount that has become receivable by the partnership and in respect of which the consideration given by the partnership therefor was property (other than property referred to in paragraph 59(2)(a), (c) or (d) of the Act or a share or interest therein or right thereto) or services, all or part of the original cost of which to the partnership may reasonably be regarded primarily as an exploration or development expense of the taxpayer, shall be deemed to be an amount receivable by the taxpayer to the extent of his share thereof, and the consideration so given by the partnership shall, to the extent of the taxpayer’s share thereof, be deemed to have been given by the taxpayer for the amount deemed to be receivable by him;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: any expenditure incurred or deemed to have been incurred by the partnership shall be deemed to have been incurred by the taxpayer to the extent of the taxpayer’s share thereof; and

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: any amount or expenditure deemed by paragraph (d) or (e) to have been receivable or incurred, as the case may be, by the taxpayer shall be deemed to have become receivable or been incurred, as the case may be, by the taxpayer on the day the amount became receivable or the expenditure was incurred or deemed to have been incurred by the partnership.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of sections 1201 to 1203, 1205, 1217 and 1218, where a taxpayer was a member of a partnership at the end of a fiscal period of the partnership, the taxpayer shall be deemed to receive or to become entitled to receive any amount of assistance or benefit, whether such amount is by way of a grant, subsidy, rebate, forgivable loan, deduction from royalty or tax, rebate of royalty or tax, investment allowance or any other form of assistance or benefit, that the partnership at any time receives or becomes entitled to receive in respect of expenses incurred in that fiscal period of the partnership, to the extent of,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: where the partnership in the fiscal period receives or becomes entitled to receive the amount, the taxpayer’s share thereof, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: where the partnership after the fiscal period becomes entitled to receive the amount, what would have been the taxpayer’s share thereof if the partnership had in the fiscal period received or become entitled to receive the amount,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: and the time at which the taxpayer is deemed to receive or become entitled to receive such share of the amount shall be the time that the partnership receives or becomes entitled to receive the amount.

Subsection.Text: Where an expense incurred after November 7, 1969 that was a Canadian exploration and development expense or that would have been such an expense if it had been incurred after 1971 (other than an amount included therein that is in respect of financing or the cost of any Canadian resource property acquired by a joint exploration corporation or any property acquired by a joint exploration corporation that would have been a Canadian resource property if it had been acquired after 1971), a Canadian exploration expense (other than an amount included therein that is in respect of financing) or a Canadian development expense (other than an amount included therein that is in respect of financing or an amount referred to in subparagraph 66.2(5)(a)(iii) of the Act) has been renounced in favour of a taxpayer and was deemed to be an expense of the taxpayer for the purposes of subsection 66(10), (10.1) or (10.2) of the Act or subsection 29(7) of the Income Tax Application Rules, the expense shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: for the purposes of sections 1203 and 1205, be deemed to have been such an expense incurred by the taxpayer at the time the expense was incurred by the joint exploration corporation; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: for the purposes of sections 1204 and 1210 and paragraphs 1217(2)(e) and 1218(2)(e), be deemed to have been such an expense incurred by the taxpayer at the time it was deemed to have been incurred by the taxpayer for the purposes of subsection 66(10), (10.1) or (10.2) of the Act or subsection 29(7) of the Income Tax Application Rules, as the case may be.

Subsection.Text: An expense that is a Canadian exploration and development overhead expense of the joint exploration corporation referred to in subsection (4), or would be such an expense if the references to “connected with the taxpayer” in paragraph (d) of the definition Canadian exploration and development overhead expense in subsection (1) were read as “connected with the shareholder corporation in favour of whom the expense was renounced for the purposes of subsection 66(10.1) or (10.2) of the Act”, that may reasonably be considered to be included in a Canadian exploration expense or Canadian development expense that is deemed by subsection (4) to be a Canadian exploration expense or Canadian development expense of the shareholder corporation, shall be deemed to be a Canadian exploration and development overhead expense of the shareholder corporation incurred by it at the time the expense was deemed by subsection (4) to have been incurred by it and shall be deemed at and after that time not to be a Canadian exploration and development overhead expense incurred by the joint exploration corporation.
For the purposes of paragraphs 66(12.6)(b), (12.601)(d) and (12.62)(b) of the Act, a prescribed Canadian exploration and development overhead expense of a corporation is

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a Canadian exploration and development overhead expense of the corporation;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: an expense that would be a Canadian exploration and development overhead expense of the corporation if the references to “connected with the taxpayer” in paragraph (d) of the definition Canadian exploration and development overhead expense in subsection (1) were read as “connected with the person to whom the expense is renounced under subsection 66(12.6), (12.601) or (12.62) of the Act”; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: an expense that would be a Canadian exploration and development overhead expense of the corporation if the references to “person who was connected with the taxpayer” in paragraph (d) of the definition Canadian exploration and development overhead expense in subsection (1) were read as “person to whom the expense is renounced under subsection 66(12.6), (12.601) or (12.62) of the Act”.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of subsections (4.2) and (5), a partnership shall be deemed to be a person and its taxation year shall be deemed to be its fiscal period.
For the purposes of subsection (6) and the definition Canadian exploration and development overhead expense in subsection (1),

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a person and a particular corporation are connected with each other if

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the person and the particular corporation are not dealing at arm’s length,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the person has an equity percentage in the particular corporation that is not less than 10 per cent, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: the person is a corporation in which another person has an equity percentage that is not less than 10 per cent and the other person has an equity percentage in the particular corporation that is not less than 10 per cent;

Paragraph.Label: (a.1)
Paragraph.Text: a person and another person that is not a corporation are connected with each other if they are not dealing at arm’s length; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: “costs incurred by a person” shall not include

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: an outlay or expense described in any of paragraphs (a) to (c) of that definition made or incurred by the person if the references in those paragraphs to “taxpayer” were read as references to “person”,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: an outlay or expense made or incurred by the person to the extent that it is not reasonably attributable to the use of a property by, the performance of a service for, or any materials, parts, or supplies acquired by, the taxpayer referred to in that definition, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: an amount in respect of the capital cost to the person of a property, other than, where the property is a depreciable property of the person, that proportion of the capital allowance of the person for his taxation year in respect of the property that may reasonably be considered attributable to the use of the property by, or in the performance of a service for, the taxpayer referred to in that definition.

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of subparagraph (5)(b)(iii), the capital allowance of a person (in this subsection referred to as the “owner”) for his taxation year in respect of a property owned by him means that proportion of an amount not exceeding 20 per cent of the amount that is

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a property owned by the owner on December 31, 1980, the lesser of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the capital cost of the property to the owner computed as if no amount had been included therein that is a cost of borrowing capital, including any cost incurred prior to the commencement of carrying on a business, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the fair market value of the property on December 31, 1980,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a property acquired by the owner after December 31, 1980 that was previously owned by a person connected with the owner, the lesser of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the capital cost of the property, computed as if no amount had been included therein that is a cost of borrowing capital, including any cost incurred prior to the commencement of carrying on a business, to the person, who was connected with the owner, who was the first person to acquire the property from a person with whom the owner was not connected, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the fair market value of the property at the time it was acquired by the owner, and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: in any other case, the capital cost of the property to the owner computed as if no amount had been included therein that is a cost of borrowing capital, including any cost incurred prior to the commencement of carrying on a business,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: that the number of days in the taxation year during which the property was owned by the owner is of 365.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of paragraph (5)(a), equity percentage has the meaning assigned by paragraph 95(4)(b) of the Act.
For the purposes of the definition qualified tertiary oil recovery project in subsection (1), a specified royalty provision means:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the Experimental Project Petroleum Royalty Regulation of Alberta (Alta. Reg. 36/79);

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: The Experimental Oil Sands Royalty Regulations of Alberta (Alta. Reg. 287/77);

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: section 4.2 of the Petroleum Royalty Regulations of Alberta (Alta. Reg. 93/74);

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: section 58A of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulations, 1969 of Saskatchewan (Saskatchewan Regulation 8/69);

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: section 204 of The Freehold Oil And Gas Production Tax Regulations, 1983 of Saskatchewan (Saskatchewan Regulation 11/83);

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: item 9 of section 2 of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Royalty Regulations of British Columbia (B.C. Reg. 549/78);

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: the Freehold Mineral Taxation Act of Alberta;

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: the Freehold Mineral Rights Tax Act of Alberta;

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: Order in Council 427/84 pursuant to section 9(a) of the Mines and Minerals Act of Alberta;

Paragraph.Label: (j)
Paragraph.Text: Order in Council 966/84 pursuant to section 9 of the Mines and Minerals Act of Alberta; or

Paragraph.Label: (k)
Paragraph.Text: Order in Council 870/84 pursuant to section 9 of the Mines and Minerals Act of Alberta.

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of paragraph (a) of the definition qualified tertiary oil recovery project in subsection (1), a specified royalty provision is deemed to apply as of a particular time if, at the particular time, unconditional approval for the specified royalty provision to apply at a time after the particular time is given by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: Her Majesty in right of Canada or of a province;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: an agent of Her Majesty in right of Canada or of a province; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a corporation, a commission or an association that is controlled by Her Majesty in right of Canada or of a province or by an agent of Her Majesty in right of Canada or of a province.

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Subsection.Text: A taxpayer may deduct in computing his income for a taxation year such amount as he may claim not exceeding the lesser of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: his income for the year, computed in accordance with Part I of the Act, if no deduction were allowed under this subsection; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: his frontier exploration base as of the end of the year (before making any deduction under this subsection for the year).

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this section, frontier exploration base of a taxpayer as of a particular time means the amount by which the aggregate of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the aggregate of all amounts, each of which is an amount in respect of a particular oil or gas well in Canada equal to 66 2/3 per cent of the amount by which

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: expenses incurred after March, 1977 and before April, 1980 and before the particular time in respect of the well (other than expenses that may reasonably be regarded as having been incurred as consideration for services rendered to the taxpayer after March, 1980) if those expenses would be included in the Canadian exploration expense of the taxpayer within the meaning of paragraph 66.1(6)(a) of the Act (if that paragraph were read without reference to subparagraphs (iii) and (iii.1) thereof and without reference to the words “within six months after the end of the year, the drilling of the well is completed and” in subparagraph (ii) thereof, and if the reference in subparagraphs (iv) and (v) thereof to “any of subparagraphs (i) to (iii.1)” were read as a reference to “subparagraph (i) or (ii)”) other than

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: a cost of borrowing capital, including any cost incurred prior to the commencement of carrying on a business, that was a Canadian exploration expense of the taxpayer,

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: an expense renounced by the taxpayer under subsection 66(10.1) of the Act,

Clause.Label: (C)
Clause.Text: an amount that, by virtue of subparagraph 66.1(6)(a)(iv) of the Act, was a Canadian exploration expense, if such amount was an expense referred to in clause (A) or (B) that was incurred by a partnership referred to in that subparagraph, or

Clause.Label: (D)
Clause.Text: an amount that, by virtue of subparagraph 66.1(6)(a)(v) of the Act, was a Canadian exploration expense, if such amount was an expense referred to in clause (A) or (B) that the taxpayer incurred pursuant to an agreement referred to in that subparagraph,

ContinuedParagraph.Text: exceeds

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the taxpayer’s threshold amount in respect of the well, minus the amount that would be determined under subparagraph (i) in respect of the taxpayer for the well if the reference therein to “after March, 1977 and before April, 1980” were read as “after June, 1976 and before April, 1977”, and

Paragraph.Label: (a.1)
Paragraph.Text: where the taxpayer is a successor corporation, any amount required by paragraph (7)(a) to be added before the particular time in computing the taxpayer’s frontier exploration base,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: exceeds the aggregate of

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: all amounts deducted by the taxpayer under subsection (1) in computing his income for taxation years ending before the particular time,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: 66 2/3 per cent of the aggregate of all amounts, each of which is an amount that became receivable by the taxpayer after March 28, 1979 and before the earlier of December 12, 1979 and the particular time, and in respect of which the consideration given by the taxpayer therefor was a property (other than a share, or a property that would have been a Canadian resource property if it had been acquired by the taxpayer at the time the consideration was given) or services the cost of which may reasonably be regarded as having been primarily an expenditure in respect of an oil or gas well for which an amount was added in computing the taxpayer’s frontier exploration base by virtue of paragraph (a) or in computing the frontier exploration base of a predecessor by virtue of paragraph (a) as it applied to the predecessor where the taxpayer is a successor corporation to the predecessor, as the case may be; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: where the taxpayer is a predecessor, any amount required by paragraph (7)(b) to be deducted before the particular time in computing the taxpayer’s frontier exploration base.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of subparagraph (2)(a)(ii), a taxpayer’s threshold amount in respect of an oil or gas well means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: where the taxpayer and one or more other persons have filed an agreement with the Minister in prescribed form in respect of the well and

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount allocated to each such person in the agreement does not exceed the amount that would be determined, at the time the agreement is filed, under subparagraph (2)(a)(i) in respect of that person for the well, if the reference in that subparagraph to “March, 1977” were read as “June, 1976”, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the aggregate of the amounts allocated by the agreement is $5 million,

ContinuedParagraph.Text: the amount allocated to the taxpayer in the agreement, but if no amount is allocated to the taxpayer in the agreement, nil;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: where such an agreement has been filed in respect of the well by one or more persons other than the taxpayer, nil; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: where no such agreement has been filed in respect of the well, $5 million.

Subsection.Text: Where as a result of mechanical or geological difficulties the drilling of a particular oil or gas well does not achieve its stated geological objectives under the drilling authority issued by the relevant government body and a further well, including a relief well, is drilled on the same geological formation and may reasonably be regarded as a continuation of or a substitution for the particular oil or gas well, the expenses in respect of the drilling of the further well shall, for the purposes of this section, be deemed to be expenses in respect of the drilling of the particular oil or gas well.
For the purposes of this section,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: when a shareholder corporation is deemed to have incurred a Canadian exploration expense by virtue of an election made by a joint exploration corporation pursuant to subsection 66(10.1) of the Act, that expense shall be deemed to have been incurred by the shareholder corporation at the time when it was incurred by the joint exploration corporation; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: when a member of a partnership is deemed to have incurred a Canadian exploration expense by virtue of subparagraph 66.1(6)(a)(iv) of the Act, that expense shall be deemed to have been incurred by the member at the time when it was incurred by the partnership.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this section, oil or gas well means any well drilled for the purpose of producing petroleum or natural gas or of determining the existence, location, extent or quality of an accumulation of petroleum or natural gas, other than a mineral resource.

Subject to subsections 1202(5) and (6), where a corporation (in this section referred to as the “successor corporation”) has at any time (in this subsection referred to as the “time of acquisition”) after April 19, 1983 and in a taxation year (in this subsection referred to as the “transaction year”) acquired a property from another person (in this subsection referred to as the “predecessor”), the following rules apply:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: for the purpose of computing the frontier exploration base of the successor corporation as of any time after the time of acquisition, there shall be added an amount equal to the amount required by paragraph (b) to be deducted in computing the frontier exploration base of the predecessor; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: for the purpose of computing the frontier exploration base of the predecessor as of any time after the transaction year of the predecessor, there shall be deducted the amount, if any, by which

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the frontier exploration base of the predecessor immediately after the time of acquisition (assuming for this purpose that, in the case of an acquisition as a result of an amalgamation described in section 87 of the Act, the predecessor existed after the time of acquisition and no property was acquired or disposed of in the course of the amalgamation)

ContinuedParagraph.Text: exceeds

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount, if any, deducted under subsection (1) in computing the income of the predecessor for the transaction year of the predecessor.

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Heading.TitleText: Additional Allowances in Respect of Certain Oil or Gas Wells

Subsection.Text: Subject to subsections (3) and (4) where a taxpayer has income for a taxation year from an oil or gas well that is outside Canada, or where an individual has income for a taxation year from an oil or gas well in Canada, in computing his income for the year he may deduct the lesser of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the aggregate of drilling costs incurred by him in that year and previous taxation years in respect of the well (not including the cost of land, leases or other rights and not including indirect expenses such as general exploration, geological and geophysical expenses) minus the aggregate of all amounts deductible in respect thereof in computing his income for previous years; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: that part of his income for the year that may reasonably be regarded as income from the well.

Subsection.Text: Where a taxpayer has more than one oil or gas well to which subsection (1) applies, the allowance in respect of the drilling costs of each well shall be computed separately.

Where an individual has income for a taxation year from an oil or gas well in Canada, no deduction may be made under this section in computing such income in respect of drilling costs of that well incurred after April 10, 1962.

Where a taxpayer has income for a taxation year from an oil or gas well that is outside Canada, no deduction may be made under this section in computing such income in respect of drilling costs of that well incurred after 1971.

Heading.TitleText: Additional Allowances in Respect of Certain Mines

Subsection.Text: Subject to subsection (3), where a taxpayer operates in Canada a mine for the production of materials from a resource he may deduct, in computing his income for a taxation year, such amount as he may claim not exceeding 25 per cent of the amount computed under subsection (2).

The amount referred to in subsection (1) is the aggregate of all expenditures made or incurred by the taxpayer before 1972 that are reasonably attributable to the prospecting and exploration for and the development of the mine prior to the coming into production of the mine in reasonable commercial quantities, except to the extent that the expenditures were

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: expenditures in respect of which a deduction from, or in computing, a taxpayer’s income tax or excess profits tax was provided by section 8 of the Income War Tax Act;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: expenditures in respect of which an amount was deducted in computing a taxpayer’s income under section 16 of chapter 63, S.C., 1947 or section 16 of chapter 53, S.C., 1947-48 or, if the expenditure was incurred prior to 1953, under section 53 of chapter 25, S.C., 1949 (Second Session);

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: expenditures incurred after 1952 in respect of which a deduction was or is provided by section 53 of chapter 25, S.C., 1949 (Second Session), section 83A of the Act as it read in its application to the 1971 taxation year or section 29 of the Income Tax Application Rules,

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: expenditures deducted in computing the income of the taxpayer in the year they were incurred;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: the cost to the taxpayer of property in respect of which an allowance is provided under paragraph 20(1)(a) of the Act; or

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: the cost to the taxpayer of a leasehold interest.

Subsection.Text: The amount deductible under subsection (1) shall not exceed the amount computed under subsection (2) minus the aggregate of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: amounts deducted under subsection (1) in computing the income of the taxpayer for previous taxation years; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: similar amounts deducted in computing the income of the taxpayer for the purposes of the Income War Tax Act and The 1948 Income Tax Act (as defined in paragraph 12(d) of the Income Tax Application Rules).
